short: The public entry, the controls, the seam, the icons, the styles and the surfaces
is: What `@zurfur/ui` ships: `index.ts`, the whole public surface of the code, and the folders behind it: `controls/`, `icons/`, `environment/` (the seam), `motion/` (the paper moves), `styles/` and `surfaces/`.
conventions: `index.ts` is the only way in. It exports the paper lists, the environment names and `parseSkin`, the token model, Icon with its names, the eleven controls, the link, day and locale mints, the item shapes, the nine surfaces with their shapes, the feedback action's shape, the picture and pin-point mints (`ImageSrc`, `PinPoint`), and the seam's types, its still forms and `provideEnvironment`. It never exports `useEnvironment` (components reach it by relative path) and never a type from bits-ui or the date library; `checks/public-entry.svelte.spec.ts` holds the exact list, so an export is added there too.

Every component here is simple or composite, as `src/checks/composition-table.ts` says, and `src/checks/composition.spec.ts` holds every file under `src/` to it, so a new export fails until it has a kind. A simple component does one job: it draws one piece itself, its own element and its own family class, and holds only glyphs (Icon, and Spinner by the literal `kind="glyph"`) and the internal pieces (FieldFrame, Tooltip). A composite only lays out library components, simple or composite, with its own family class and plain text: it renders no button, link, field, picture or frame of its own. The owned elements (`button`, `a`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `img`, `video`, `audio`, `iframe`, SVG `image`), each `zf-` family and each bits-ui name stay with the files the table lists; bits-ui's link and image parts stay with none, and no file here renders `link`, `base`, `<svelte:head>` or a nested `<style>`. Each family has one stylesheet row, and none when its component styles it in its own `<style>`; every stylesheet under `lib/` is read, one in a `styles/` folder by its row and any other only for `zf-sr`. No file here imports the package entry (`index`, the folder, `$lib` or `@zurfur/ui`). The named exceptions only shrink.

`src/checks/composition-table.ts` and `eslint.config.js`'s file lists are security-trigger files: a change that adds a row (a kind, a family, an exception, an owner of an owned element, a bits-ui name, or a file in an eslint list) gets a security review.

Everything here is dumb: no fetch and no remote strings, no stores, no module-level `let`, `new Map` or `Set`, `$state` or `$derived` in a `.ts` or `.js` file, no `<script module>`, no `$app/*` and no clock reads. Seam constants are frozen. A `.svelte.ts` or `.svelte.js` file lives only in `motion/`.

Svelte's context lives only in `environment/`; the shipped tier may not call `provideEnvironment`. Motion libraries are imported only in `motion/`, and heavy libraries only by dynamic import in `lazy/`, which does not exist yet.
bits-ui and `@internationalized/date` are imported only by `.svelte` files here, never by a `.ts` file, the gallery, a route or a check harness, and no control passes one of their types out.
The seam files and the second-change rule are described in `environment/`.

fs.name: controls/
fs.role: the eleven controls, their item shapes, the link, day and locale mints, and the row stepper

fs.name: environment/
fs.role: the seam: moves, sounds and the one context that carries them

fs.name: motion/
fs.role: paper-moves.css (the paper moves, the motion adapter's CSS half) and paper-moves.ts (`PAPER_MOVES`); only a later adapter applies the move classes

fs.name: styles/
fs.role: design tokens, the two skins, the paper look, and the family stylesheets of the controls and the surfaces

fs.name: surfaces/
fs.role: the surfaces and feedback pieces (nine simple ones today), their shapes and run-time choices, and the picture and pin-point mints
